title: Sweep-and-wear-level KV allocator to mitigate GPU fragmentation
creator: Aisha Marlow
description:
Problem: Long-running model endpoints accumulate KV cache fragmentation across multiple model versions and varying sequence lengths. Fragmentation increases peak GPU memory and causes forced evictions, latency spikes, and reduced throughput. Existing work (regional compaction, slab packs) reduces fragmentation but either requires heavy pause-the-world operations or inefficient overprovisioning.

Goal: Implement a low-latency, incremental compaction and allocation policy ("sweep-and-wear-level allocator") for the KV cache that reduces fragmentation without large stop-the-world passes and without materially increasing per-request latency. The approach blends epoch-based residency scoring, wear-level allocation (spread writes across pools to avoid hot slots), and opportunistic micro-compaction during idle SM cycles and orchestration quiescence windows.

Scope: Prototype and ship runtime changes that (1) introduce a residency score used by the eviction policy, (2) implement a micro-sweeper that coalesces small free segments when GPU utilization is low, (3) modify allocator to prefer wear-level placement for new KV slabs, and (4) add diagnostic telemetry for fragmentation, sweeps, and compaction latency.

Out of scope: Full in-memory relocation requiring cross-device migration and live token cache translation across model variants. Cross-server migrations will be tracked in a follow-up ticket.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after weekly runtime triage; reproducer traced to 99th-percentile long-tail allocations on chat workloads.
2026-03-11: Spike completed - benchmark harness simulating mixed seq-length traffic and background writes. Observed fragmentation ratio increase ~22% over 72 hours on default allocator.
2026-03-12: Design doc (first draft) posted to Confluence with algorithm sketches and latency trade-off matrix (link below).

2026-03-13: Prototype allocator implemented in experiment branch: wear-level placement + epoch scoring. Micro-sweeper run integrated with runtime idle hook. Internal perf run shows 8% reduction in peak memory footprint and no >1ms p99 addl latency under moderate load.
2026-03-14: Code review opened (PR #1286). Need to validate under heavy throughput (dedicated pools) and add more telemetry for compaction-induced stalls.
decisions: Use epoch-based residency score (age + access frequency) rather than pure LRU to prioritize compaction candidates.
Micro-sweeps will run opportunistically when GPU SM utilization < 35% for 200ms to avoid impacting latency-sensitive windows.
Wear-level allocator will round-robin initial slab placement across N micro-pools per GPU (configurable, default N=8) to reduce hot-slot buildup.
Avoid full-page relocation for v1; instead, implement in-place coalescing of adjacent free segments plus compact-on-read hints for hot objects.
Telemetry added to runtime metrics: fragmentation_ratio, micro_sweeps_count, average_sweep_time_ms, residency_score_histogram.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled perf runs show >=6% reduction in peak GPU KV memory across 72-hour mixed workload replay without increasing p99 latency by >2ms.
No regressions on throughput on dedicated pools (within 3% of baseline) under steady-state load.
Micro-sweeper respects idle policy (does not run during latency-critical windows) and can be toggled via runtime flag.
New telemetry surfaces in Console: fragmentation ratio and sweep events per-host for troubleshooting.
Code merged and feature gated behind runtime flag; rollout plan documented with canary thresholds.
